E021-01.notes: No punctuation between subject (junior named Dana Ruiz) and verb 'helped'; comma, semicolon, dash all split subject from verb.

E021-02.notes: Small range contrasted with large population calls for 'but'; so/for/and so give wrong cause-effect logic.

E021-03.notes: Relative pronoun is subject of 'had planned' -> 'who'; 'whom' is the object-case trap, 'which' is for things, 'whose' possessive.

E021-05.notes: The announcement hour is itself a program on the station, so the comparison needs 'any other program'; A/B illogically compare it to itself, D changes meaning (more than all programs combined).

E021-06.notes: 'running on a generator' is a nonessential phrase needing paired commas; B drops the closing comma, C semicolon creates fragment, D 'and' leaves no main verb structure.

E021-07.notes: Redundancy: 'consecutive' and 'in a row' repeat each other; 'three days' is concise. C and D still redundant/wordy.

E021-08.notes: 'they' could refer to commissioners or volunteers; naming 'the commissioners' removes ambiguity. 'it' wrong number, 'those' unclear.

flags: minor: the sentence would be placed after the storm/aftermath narrative concludes, so 'interrupts the account of the storm' is slightly loose; still clearly the best choice since the detail is irrelevant there
E021-09.notes: Call-letter detail is irrelevant to the storm/generator paragraph; A/B misstate its function, C claims a nonexistent contradiction.

E021-10.notes: Essay shows the station becoming a community bulletin board and sole news source during the storm; B/C misstate content, D is irrelevant reasoning.
